title: Forms of Energy: Analysis and Investigation
subject: Science

questions.question: A student investigates how the number of batteries affects the brightness of a bulb. What is the changed variable?
questions.explanation: The changed variable is the one the student intentionally changes to test its effect. Here, the student changes the number of batteries.

questions.question: In the same experiment (number of batteries vs bulb brightness), what is the measured variable?
questions.explanation: The measured variable is the result observed or measured. The brightness changes in response to the number of batteries.

questions.question: To ensure a fair test in the battery experiment, which variable must be kept the same?
questions.explanation: Fixed variables must be kept constant to ensure a fair test. The type of bulb must remain the same so only the batteries affect the brightness.

questions.question: Data shows: 1 battery (Dim), 2 batteries (Bright), 3 batteries (Very Bright). What is the relationship?
options: As the number of batteries increases, the brightness decreases.
As the number of batteries increases, the brightness increases.
The number of batteries does not affect brightness.
As the brightness increases, the number of batteries decreases.
questions.explanation: The pattern shows that more batteries provide more electrical energy, resulting in a brighter bulb.

questions.question: Which energy conversion chain correctly represents a hydroelectric power station?
questions.explanation: Water at height (Potential) falls to gain speed (Kinetic), turning turbines to generate electricity (Electrical).

questions.question: Plants make food using sunlight. Animals eat plants to run. What is the energy pathway?
questions.explanation: Plants convert Light energy to energy stored in food. Animals convert energy from food into Kinetic energy for movement.

questions.question: Two identical balls are dropped from different heights. Ball A from 1m, Ball B from 2m. Which has more potential energy at the start?
questions.explanation: Potential energy depends on height. Ball B is higher, so it has more potential energy than Ball A.

questions.question: When Ball B (from previous question) hits the ground, it makes a louder sound than Ball A. Why?
options: Ball B converted more potential energy into kinetic and sound energy
Ball A lost its energy in the air
Sound energy is not related to height
questions.explanation: Ball B started with more potential energy, which converted to more kinetic energy. Upon impact, more energy was converted into sound and heat.

questions.question: An appliance is said to be 'energy efficient'. What does this mean?
options: It converts more input energy into useful output energy.
It works slower than other appliances.
questions.explanation: Energy efficiency means less energy is wasted (e.g., as heat) and more is converted into the useful form (e.g., light or motion).

questions.question: Why do we repeat experiments three times and take an average?
options: To make the experiment take longer
To ensure the results are reliable and accurate
questions.explanation: Repeating experiments helps to minimize errors and ensures the results are consistent and reliable.

questions.question: A pendulum swings from Position A (highest) to Position B (lowest). Where is kinetic energy maximum?
questions.explanation: At the lowest point (B), all potential energy has converted to kinetic energy, so speed and kinetic energy are maximum.

questions.question: Why does a pendulum eventually stop swinging?
options: It runs out of potential energy permanently
Energy is lost to the surroundings as heat and sound due to air resistance and friction
questions.explanation: Energy is not destroyed but converted to useless forms (heat/sound) due to friction/air resistance, leaving less energy for motion.

questions.question: Which modification would increase the kinetic energy of a moving trolley?
questions.explanation: Kinetic energy depends on motion. Increasing the speed increases the kinetic energy. Lifting it increases potential energy.

questions.question: In a circuit, wires become warm after being switched on for a while. What energy conversion causes this?
questions.explanation: Some electrical energy is always converted to heat energy due to resistance in the wires. This is often wasted energy.

questions.question: How does using less electrical energy help the environment?
options: It reduces the burning of fossil fuels in power stations, reducing pollution
It increases the cost of electricity
It stops the Sun from shining
questions.explanation: Many power stations burn fossil fuels to generate electricity. Using less reduces fuel consumption and pollution (greenhouse gases).
